poster_title: Expanding RL with Verifiable Rewards Across Diverse Domains
authors: Yi Su, Dian Yu, Linfeng Song, Juntao Li, Haitao Mi, Zhaopeng Tu, Min Zhang, Dong Yu

content: RLVR enhances reasoning capabilities of LLMs in structured tasks.
Challenges in verifying complex, unstructured reference answers.
Binary verification signals limit application in unstructured tasks.
Resource-intensive domain-specific annotation for reward models.
60.3% of mathematical problems have single-term numerical answers.
45.4% of multi-domain queries have verifiable answers by rule-based methods.
Need for scalable and robust reward signals in diverse domains.
Generative scoring for soft, model-based reward signals.
Training 7B LLMs as cross-domain generative reward models.
Using data from RL exploration supervised by a larger teacher model.
Conducted experiments in medicine, chemistry, psychology, economics, and education.
Used free-form, unstructured answers by domain experts for verification.
Outperformed Qwen2.5-72B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B in free-form settings.
Achieved up to 8.0% accuracy boost in diverse reasoning tasks.
Model-based soft rewards produced more robust policies.
Enhanced robustness, flexibility, and scalability of RLVR in complex scenarios.
Step towards practical RL applications in diverse, real-world domains.
